solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Negative element in county team

parts.note: County Down, in Northern Ireland
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is spoiling a county sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A downside is the disadvantage or drawback of something, its negative aspect.

clue.text: Guardian's charge put up in no-win situation

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading its letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a ward is a minor placed in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: A guardian's fee is raised in a contest nobody won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee; here it is the person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is a game or match that ends level, with neither side winning.

clue.text: What's sound engineer accomplished in improving things on tracks?

definitions.text: engineer accomplished in improving things on tracks

indicators.note: 'what's sound' asks for what the word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: the question word is pronounced the same as the engineer's surname

explanation.surface: A question about which skilled engineer improved railway equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's sound' reads as a question but means the sound of the word 'what'.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt, the Scottish engineer, greatly improved the steam engine, which went on to power locomotives on railway tracks.

clue.text: Drink daily, cause of depression

parts.note: The Sun is a daily newspaper
a downer is something that makes you gloomy

explanation.surface: Drinking every day leads to depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink daily' reads as a habit, but 'daily' is the newspaper The Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, the end of the working day.

clue.text: Political prognostication, piece of wisdom I, not he or you, needed

indicators.note: a piece of the following words is taken, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.words: wisdom I, not he or you
parts.note: the letters run from the end of wisdom across to the start of you

explanation.surface: A political forecast built on a nugget of wisdom about oneself rather than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like the domino itself, which is a red herring; the whole answer lies hidden across six words.
explanation.definitionFit: The domino theory was the Cold War prediction that one country falling to communism would make its neighbours follow.

clue.text: Combination of blood groups that's found in African forest

definitions.note: the definition describes the tree rather than naming it

parts.note: blood group B
blood group A
blood group O
blood group B again
blood group AB

explanation.surface: A mixture of blood types discovered in an African jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination' is only a joining instruction: the four ABO groups B, A, O, B and AB are written one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a huge, thick-trunked tree native to Africa.

clue.text: Old weapon found in a river bank

parts.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river
a bank or row of seats, keys or similar

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon discovered on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River bank' reads as one place but splits into river and bank, a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrows, shot from bows, were a standard missile weapon long before firearms.

clue.text: Hard to learn under coach that's venomous creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the earlier wordplay beneath what follows, so the coach comes first

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
H for hard, as on pencils
to master a skill is to learn it fully

explanation.surface: Something hard to learn under a sports coach turns out to be venomous.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under coach' places the hard-to-learn letters below the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushmaster is a large, highly venomous pit viper of Central and South America.

clue.text: Crazy family that requires careful steps

parts.note: going bananas means going mad
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A mad family that needs handling with care.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: you watch where you step to avoid slipping on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is the classic slipping hazard, and figuratively any potential embarrassment needing caution.

clue.text: Nation confused by the writer's contradiction

indicators.note: a confused word has its letters muddled into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's is my

explanation.surface: A country thrown into confusion by an author's inconsistency.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinomy is a contradiction between two beliefs or conclusions that each seem reasonable.

clue.text: Where most have convictions, image improvement is working

parts.note: PR, public relations, polishes an image
taken as written
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Image-building works best where people hold strong beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convictions' suggests firm beliefs, but the definition means criminal convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly everyone in a jail has been found guilty of a crime, so the inmates have convictions.

clue.text: Kind of Christian convert best in prayer

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: all three words are used as letters

explanation.surface: Advice that a religious convert is best at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' sits naturally with Christian, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Presbyterians are Protestants whose church is governed by elders, as in the Church of Scotland.

clue.text: Reckon railway signal's broken by wife or other females in same state

indicators.note: something broken by an intruder has that intruder lodged inside it

parts.note: to count is to reckon up
RY is the abbreviation for railway
W for wife
an omen is a sign of what is coming

explanation.surface: A broken railway signal interrupted by a wife or other women.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside RYOMEN, between railway and signal. The definition means women from the same nation as oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Your countrywomen are women of your own country, fellow female citizens of the same state.

clue.text: Socrates I'd badly punished in Greek way

indicators.note: done badly, the words are mangled and their letters end up out of order

parts.note: the philosopher's name plus the contraction

explanation.surface: Socrates claims he was punished harshly by the Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: Socrates was in fact executed by Athens, not banished, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism was the Athenian practice of voting a citizen into ten years' exile by writing names on potsherds.

clue.text: Spice, say, for about pound

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: being for something is favouring it
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: A spice used to stand in for a pound of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks spice as an example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Spice is one example of a flavouring, a substance added to food to give taste.

clue.text: Wise man adding name to one's performance

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one person
N for name

explanation.surface: A sage adds his name to a one-man show.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the Athenian lawgiver, and his name is used for any wise legislator or sage.

clue.text: Tax lots of wine — such actions have lasting consequences

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or test them
wine is sold by the case

explanation.surface: Duty on large wine orders has long-term effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actions' means lawsuits; a test case sets a precedent for later rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose verdict becomes a precedent governing many later disputes.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink that's sold in bars

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hot cocoa drink
second meaning: confectionery moulded into blocks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs, where a soft drink would be an odd order; here the bars are slabs of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hot cocoa drink and the sweet sold in slabs.

clue.text: Eg Eliot's work in bank, in opposite sense

indicators.note: in places one thing inside the other

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
T. S. Eliot wrote poetry

explanation.surface: A poet's writing kept in a bank, read the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb: to bank on is to rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversely means the other way round, in a contrary or opposite direction or sense.

clue.text: After zero, mostly call into question critical marks

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
to belie is to show something false or contradict it

explanation.surface: Having scored nothing, a critic queries the marks given.
explanation.walkthrough: Obeli are the dagger or division-sign marks used by scholars editing texts.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is a mark used by textual critics to flag a doubtful or spurious passage.

clue.text: Highly distinctive singer getting note wrong right after bar

parts.note: a counter is the bar in a shop or pub

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R for right

explanation.surface: A singer hits a wrong note straight after a bar of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a bar of music, but it is a counter; 'highly' in the definition points to the very high voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A countertenor is a male singer whose voice reaches the alto range, high and unusual.

clue.text: In that situation, it's repeatedly said to be comforting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at that place or point

definitions.text: it's repeatedly said to be comforting
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word said twice to soothe someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'There, there' is what you say to comfort someone upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at that place, and doubled it is a stock phrase of consolation.

clue.text: Wrestling ring with additional problem

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem, here one of addition
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wrestling ring brings an added headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' belongs with wrestling in the surface but is just the letter O, set after the sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling between heavyweights in a circular ring.

clue.text: This is the last signal to player crossing line

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so one word straddles the other

parts.note: an actor's cue tells them when to come in
L for line

explanation.surface: A final prompt is given to an actor crossing a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the clue itself, which is the last clue of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the final item in the puzzle, the thing you are reading is itself the last crossword hint.

clue.text: Small organ piece, part of larger one

parts.note: S for small
the liver is a body organ

explanation.surface: A small slice of organ meat, part of a larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliver is a thin splinter or fragment broken off something bigger.

clue.text: Like most piano music in an album I arranged

indicators.note: music is arranged, and so letters can be set out in a new order

parts.note: the three words are used as letters

explanation.surface: A pianist describes the pieces on an album they arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' fits the musical surface perfectly but is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Most piano music is written for both hands, so it is played with two hands.

clue.text: What student may achieve in sixty minutes

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a unit of angle made up of sixty minutes of arc

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sixty minutes' suggests an hour, but minutes of arc are meant: sixty of them make one unit of angle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an academic award and a unit of angular measure.

clue.text: Wild animal bound, attached to stake, initially

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A wild beast leaps while tied to a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' suggests a post an animal is tethered to; it is a gambling stake, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are swift, horned grazing mammals of Africa and Asia.
